pages: Falcon Rover Field Manual. Chapter one covers specifications. The Falcon rover is a six wheeled survey vehicle built for dry lake beds and gravel plains. Its chassis is a welded aluminium frame with a sealed electronics bay under the deck. With its standard sensor mast fitted the Falcon rover weighs 42 kg, and the mast alone adds 3 kg when it is removed and stored separately. The rover measures 110 cm long and 70 cm wide. Ground clearance is 18 cm, which allows it to cross rocks the size of a football without scraping the bay. The deck has four mounting rails for optional payloads such as soil probes or a weather station. Each wheel is driven by its own brushless motor, so the rover can keep moving if a single motor fails. The paint is a pale grey chosen to reduce heat absorption during long days in direct sun.

Chapter two covers power. The Falcon rover runs on two folding solar panels mounted on hinged arms above the deck. In full sun the panels deliver a combined 180 watts. Energy is stored in a lithium iron phosphate battery pack rated at 960 watt hours. A full battery supports about six hours of driving with no sun at all, or roughly a full day of stationary sensing. The battery must be kept between minus ten and forty five degrees Celsius; outside that range the controller stops charging to protect the cells. Operators should fold the panels flat before driving in wind stronger than forty kilometres per hour, because the hinged arms are not designed for gusts. A charging port on the rear panel accepts a standard 24 volt supply for bench charging indoors.

Chapter three covers navigation. The rover plans routes using a stereo camera pair and a satellite receiver. On flat, firm ground the top speed is 3 km/h, and the controller automatically slows to 1 km/h on slopes steeper than ten degrees. The obstacle avoidance system stops the rover when an object closer than 60 cm appears in its path, then searches for a route around it. Waypoints are uploaded as a simple list of coordinates over the field radio, which has a range of about two kilometres in open terrain. If the radio link is lost for more than five minutes, the rover returns to its last confirmed waypoint and waits for contact. Night driving is not supported because the cameras need daylight to judge distance reliably.

Chapter four covers maintenance. Inspect all six wheels every 50 hours of driving, checking the tread for cuts and the hubs for sand. Clean the camera windows with a soft cloth and distilled water before each mission. The battery pack should be replaced after about two thousand full charge cycles, or sooner if runtime drops below four hours. Motor bearings are sealed and need no lubrication. Firmware updates are installed from a memory card inserted into the slot inside the electronics bay; never interrupt an update once it starts. Store the rover indoors between field seasons with the battery charged to about half capacity.

Riverside Orchard Cooperative membership policy. Membership is open to any grower farming within the valley district. The annual membership fee is 240 credits, payable before the first of March each year. New members pay a one time joining contribution of 100 credits in addition to the annual fee. Members receive access to the shared cold storage building, the cooperative pressing equipment and the weekly market stall. Each member household has one vote at the general meeting, regardless of the size of its orchard. Membership lapses automatically if the annual fee is more than sixty days overdue.

Harvest schedule. Apple picking for early varieties begins in the second week of August, and late varieties are picked through October. Pear harvest runs from the last week of August to mid September. Members must book pressing slots at least seven days in advance through the cooperative office, and each household may book at most three pressing slots per week during peak season. Fruit delivered to cold storage must be labelled with the grower name, variety and picking date. Cold storage is kept at two degrees Celsius and the building is locked each evening at eight.

Dispute process. A member who disagrees with a decision of the committee may request a review in writing within thirty days. The review is heard by a panel of three members who did not take part in the original decision. The panel meets within twenty one days of receiving the request and gives its decision in writing. If the member is still not satisfied, the matter goes to a vote at the next general meeting, and that vote is final. Throughout the process, the member keeps full access to cooperative facilities.

Northgate community office memo. The office is open from 9 am to 4 pm on weekdays and from 10 am to 1 pm on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays and public holidays. Visitors can borrow tools from the lending shelf for up to one week by signing the register at the front desk. The printer in the side room is free for up to twenty pages per person per day.
